{"id": 5, "row_id": "f_470ae81236d5bd39045dc1", "summary": "Inserted: {"title": "match3d-backend - prod deploys", "body_text": "match3d-backend - prod deploys\nHow prod works for the ZM backend since the prod env went up (match3d-backend#2).\n\nMerging doesn't deploy an", "operation": "INSERT", "timestamp": "2026-10-27T12:38:16.800763+00:00", "table_name": "docs_documents", "schema_name": "gdocs", "changed_fields": {"title": "match3d-backend - prod deploys", "body_text": "match3d-backend - prod deploys
How prod works for the ZM backend since the prod env went up (match3d-backend#2).

Merging doesn't deploy anything. Dev is deployed by hand from main. Prod runs from the prod branch: to put a PR on prod you cherry-pick it onto prod, build a new zm-api task definition revision and update the service (steps on the CI/CD Pipeline & Branching page). Only the PRs picked onto prod are on prod.

Whoever deploys a PR to prod comments on that PR with a line starting "prod:", the time in UTC and the task definition. That comment is what puts the PR on prod, not the merge and not a Slack message.

A prod deploy only counts if the PR already had an Approve review from someone other than its author when it went out. Approving afterwards doesn't fix it; redeploy.

To roll back, revert the pick on prod, redeploy and comment "rollback:" on the PR. A rollback takes the PR off prod whenever it happens, freeze or not, until a newer "prod:" comment.

Console changes and spreadsheet imports have no PR: they go in the deploy log, Console & imports tab, with what changed or what was imported, the target (dev or prod) and the time.

Freezes: from the server freeze on the calendar until the beta ships, the Approve review has to be Arthur's. Anything else deployed during the freeze gets rolled back at go/no-go.

The deploy log also has a Prod deploys tab as a quick list.
